intro: Rows from the same person or session can leak information across a random split. A group holdout keeps every row belonging to a selected group together.
task: Create a heldout split at the group level and verify that repeated subjects never cross the boundary.
requirements: groups and heldout_groups are lists or tuples of nonempty string IDs with at most 10000 entries. groups may be empty.
Return a dictionary with train and test NumPy integer index vectors. test contains rows whose group occurs in heldout_groups; train contains the rest.
Preserve original row order, allow repeated heldout IDs, and reject heldout IDs that do not occur in groups. Empty heldout_groups puts all rows in training.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Split membership, not individual rows
hints.body: Every occurrence of a chosen group must receive the same destination.

hints.title: Enumerate the original rows
hints.body: Index outputs should follow input order rather than sorted group order.

explanation: Group-aware evaluation prevents identity or session information from appearing in both splits. The chosen holdout groups define the experimental unit, even when groups have unequal sizes.
The function only materializes a specified partition; it does not optimize group balance or choose holdout groups. Returning row indices makes the split reusable across aligned arrays.
